summary.ground_truth: Hand-written by the author. SQL cases are graded against a gold query run on the frozen ops_eval database at eval time; policy cases against the sections the author identified in data/policies; refusals and proposals against the status the loop records; the tenant case against the other restaurant's figure, which must not appear. Every case also checks that each query the guard let through was pinned to the asking restaurant.

case.question: How many catering orders did we do in October?
case.note: A catering order is one with an item from the Catering category on the menu. Nothing on the order itself says catering: no channel, no label, no discount. Three ad hoc asks on 1 November all searched the order's labels, found nothing, and said the data cannot identify catering orders. 18.
case.gold_sql:
-- sql-11: How many catering orders did we do in October?

SELECT count(DISTINCT o.id)
FROM orders o
JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id
JOIN items i ON i.id = oi.item_id
JOIN categories c ON c.id = i.category_id
WHERE o.state = 'completed'
  AND c.name = 'Catering'
  AND o.created_at >= timestamp '2026-10-01' AT TIME ZONE 'America/Chicago'
  AND o.created_at <  timestamp '2026-11-01' AT TIME ZONE 'America/Chicago'

reasons: the answer's figures are 1, 6, 17, 2,026, 24, 10, 12; none is within 1% of 18

trace.question: How many catering orders did we do in October?
trace.answer:
We did 17 catering orders in October 2026, covering October 1 through today, October 24. I counted completed orders that include at least one item from the Catering menu category. That category has six items, such as Pho Bar for 10 and Sandwich Platter for 12. The gross sales on those 17 orders total $2,880.80. That figure is the full value of each order, so it includes any non-catering items on the same order.

The house policies don't define "catering." They only set rules for it [House Policy §6, Catering], so I used the menu category.

detail.sql: select c.name cat, i.name item, i.id from items i join categories c on c.id=i.category_id where c.name ilike '%cater%' or i.name ilike '%cater%'

SELECT c.name AS cat, i.name AS item, i.id FROM (SELECT * FROM items WHERE merchant_id = 1) AS i JOIN (SELECT * FROM categories WHERE merchant_id = 1) AS c ON c.id = i.category_id WHERE c.name ILIKE '%cater%' OR i.name ILIKE '%cater%' LIMIT 500
